facts.material: electrodes (likely coated titanium) in a plastic cartridge housing (not stated)
facts.function: electrolyzes dissolved salt in spa water to generate chlorine and release it into the water
facts.form: replaceable electrolytic cell cartridge, powered by the spa's control system

gri_path: GRI 1: heading 8543 names machines and apparatus for electrolysis (8543.30); the cartridge is the electrolytic cell that performs the electrolysis, so it is the apparatus itself, not merely a part
Section XVI note 2(a): a good that is itself described by a heading (electrolysis apparatus) stays in that heading even if installed in a spa system
GRI 6: 8543.30.90 other (not for printed circuits); suffix .90 other (not hydrogen electrolyzer or magnesium anode)

rejected_alternatives.reason: the cartridge does not filter water; its function is chemical generation of chlorine by electrolysis, which heading 8543.30 names specifically
parts line; applies only if the cartridge lacks the electrodes/cell and is merely a housing or component of the electrolytic apparatus
the article is an apparatus, not a chemical disinfectant

missing_facts: Does the cartridge contain the complete electrolytic cell (electrodes) or is it only a housing/consumable part of a separately imported salt system?
classification.rationale: The FreshWater salt cartridge generates chlorine by passing current through salt water, which is electrolysis, so heading 8543 (machines and apparatus for electrolysis) describes it by GRI 1. NY F89627 (in force) confirms CBP treats chlorine-producing electrolysis machines under heading 8543 (there, their components in 8543.90). With the cell itself imported, the residual statistical line 8543.30.90.90 applies; no ruling on this exact spa cartridge was found.
